generic_name: Multivitamin with Iron (Vitamin C, Vitamin D, Vitamin E, Vitamin B6, Folate, Vitamin B12, Iron)
purpose: This combination of vitamins and minerals helps your body stay healthy and work properly every day. Each ingredient plays a special role — from keeping your bones strong and your immune system fighting, to helping your blood carry oxygen and your nerves function well. Doctors often recommend this if you are not getting enough nutrients from your diet or if you have increased needs, like during pregnancy.
how_it_works: Think of these vitamins and minerals as a team, each doing a specific job in your body. Vitamin C and E act like shields, protecting your cells from damage. Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium to keep bones strong. The B vitamins (B6, B12, and Folate) help your body make energy and keep your nerves and blood cells healthy. Iron helps your red blood cells carry oxygen throughout your body so you feel energized and not tired.
common_side_effects: Some people may notice an upset stomach, nausea, or constipation, especially if taken on an empty stomach. Iron can make your stools look darker or greenish — this is normal and not dangerous. Taking it with food usually helps reduce any stomach discomfort. High doses of Vitamin C may cause loose stools or diarrhea in some people.
warnings: Keep this product away from children — iron supplements can be very dangerous or even life-threatening if a child swallows too many. Do not take more than the recommended dose, as too much of certain vitamins (like Vitamin D and E) can build up in your body and cause harm. If you are pregnant, talk to your doctor before taking any supplement, as some doses may need to be adjusted. Let your doctor and pharmacist know about all medications you take, since iron can interfere with the absorption of some drugs like certain antibiotics and thyroid medications. People with certain conditions like hemochromatosis (iron overload disease) should avoid extra iron.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the usual dose is one tablet or capsule taken once daily, preferably with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Pregnant women may have different needs and are often given a special prenatal vitamin — always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Do not crush or chew extended-release forms unless your pharmacist says it is okay. Take iron-containing supplements a few hours apart from antacids, dairy products, or certain antibiotics for best absorption.
